chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the meats of the sacrificed animals, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) used to give in charity a third to their neighbours, and a third to the beggars, and a third they would keep for the Ahl al-Bayt.'

key_terms.لِأَهْلِ الْبَيْتِ: for the Ahl al-Bayt (the Prophet's family)

ai.seo_question: How should sacrificial meat be distributed according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the prophetic tradition of tripartite distribution of sacrificial meat, a practice attributed to Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn and Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq. It underscores the social responsibility of the Ahl al-Bayt by allocating one-third to neighbors, one-third to the poor, and retaining one-third for their own household, reflecting a balanced approach to charity and sustenance. This method serves as a practical model for Muslims to emulate in the distribution of udhiyah, emphasizing community welfare and familial provision.
